title: Historical Thai Buddhist Solar Calendar
intro: Thailand's modern Buddhist Era dates use a different year number. This historical model also remembers the former April-start year and the 1940 transition.
summary: Buddhist Era year numbers with a change from April-start to January-start years on 1 January 1941.
origin: Thailand introduced a solar civil system in 1912. The year-start change in 1941 produced an unusually short Buddhist Era year 2483.
structure: Before 1941, a Buddhist Era year began on 1 April. Buddhist Era 2483 ran only from April to December 1940, after which years began in January.
pattern_note: There is no January–March in Buddhist Era year 2483. Those dates belong to a different year, and fabricated 2483 dates must be rejected.
history: A common modern conversion adds 543 to the Gregorian year, but that shortcut alone gets some early twentieth-century Thai dates wrong because years once changed in April.
example: Gregorian 2026 is Thai Buddhist Era 2569. Gregorian October 1940 is in Buddhist Era 2483; January 1941 is already in 2484.
limits: This provider begins with the 1912 solar civil convention. It must not invent missing January–March dates in BE 2483 or treat all earlier regional calendars as the same.
